news.title: Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot
news.summary_raw:
We’re reimagining Microsoft Copilot to enable work as it evolves and to help expand what every individual and every organization can accomplish in the flow of human ambition. Today we’re introducing the new Copilot to connect the tools people rely on with the next generation of capabilities they’ll need to build, customize and scale AI...
The post Introducing the new Copilot with Home, Code and Autopilot appeared first on The Official Microsoft Blog.
news.summary: Microsoft has unveiled a new version of Copilot featuring Home, Code, and Autopilot, integrating AI into the full Microsoft ecosystem to enable users to build, customize, and scale applications more efficiently. This release expands Copilot’s capabilities across Microsoft 365, Azure, and other core services, promising deeper automation and contextual assistance for enterprise workflows.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Immediately explore the new Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center, enabling Home, Code, and Autopilot features for your tenant. S2: Delaying adoption could leave your organization behind in productivity automation, missing out on streamlined app development and AI-assisted governance. S3: Focus on the Microsoft 365 and Azure portals, as these are the primary platforms where the new Copilot will be deployed and where your team’s current tools reside.

news.title: Introducing Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar
news.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 3.8 Live with Live Avatar, a new generative AI model that supports real‑time avatar-based interactions. This update expands Gemini’s capabilities into live, multimodal experiences that can be integrated into Google Workspace and other Google Cloud services.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Review the Gemini 3.8 Live API documentation this week and evaluate enabling Live Avatar in your Google Workspace Admin console. S2: Inaction means missing early access to a feature that can streamline internal communication and enhance customer support with AI avatars, potentially reducing ticket volume. S3: Focus on Google Workspace and Google Cloud Platform, as they will host the most direct integration points for your SSO and collaboration stack.

news.title: OpenAI extends cyber access to Ukraine for civilian defense
news.summary_raw: OpenAI is extending access to its Daybreak program to the Government of Ukraine to support the cyber defense of civilian infrastructure.
news.summary: OpenAI has extended its Daybreak cyber defense program to support Ukrainian civilian infrastructure, providing advanced AI tools for threat analysis and mitigation. This move underscores the growing role of AI in national defense and the importance of AI-enabled security solutions.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Verify whether your current MDM and endpoint security tools (e.g., CrowdStrike, Cloudflare, MDM platforms) have APIs to integrate OpenAI's Daybreak or similar AI threat intelligence services. S2: Failing to incorporate AI-driven threat analysis could leave critical infrastructure exposed to sophisticated attacks, especially in high-risk regions. S3: Prioritize evaluating your existing security stack for compatibility with external AI threat feeds, and plan a phased integration within the next 30 days.

news.title: Advancing Private AI Compute with secure, server-side memory
news.summary_raw: Introducing private, server-side memory to Private AI Compute for personal AI.
news.summary: Google DeepMind has introduced private, server-side memory to its Private AI Compute platform, enabling personal AI models to retain context without exposing data to external servers. This advancement aims to keep sensitive user data within a secure environment while allowing continuous, context-aware AI interactions.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Check the new Private AI Compute API settings in the Google Cloud console this week. S2: Failing to evaluate this feature could mean missed opportunities to keep customer data internal for AI-driven support tools, potentially exposing sensitive information through third‑party services. S3: This directly impacts Google Workspace and any custom AI extensions you run on Google Cloud, offering a safer foundation for future automation.

news.title: Anthropic to pay Akamai $11.6 billion over seven years in cloud deal
news.summary_raw: Anthropic has committed $11.6 billion over seven years to Akamai's cloud infrastructure, a bet on CPUs that could grow to about $20 billion, and in an unusual arrangement, Akamai is giving Anthropic a potential stake of up to 5% of its stock that grows as Anthropic spends more.
news.summary: Anthropic has struck an $11.6 billion, seven‑year cloud infrastructure deal with Akamai, betting on CPU capacity that could expand to $20 billion and granting Anthropic a potential 5% stock stake that scales with spend. The agreement positions Akamai as a key partner for AI workloads and could reshape cloud‑compute pricing for enterprise customers.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Review the Akamai contract terms in your vendor management portal and flag any cost‑overrun clauses that could impact your cloud budgets. S2: Failure to monitor Akamai’s usage metrics could expose your organization to unanticipated CPU spikes and hidden fees that would erode cost controls. S3: This is most relevant to your Azure and AWS spend management and any MDM or SSO integrations that rely on Akamai’s edge services.

In a closed a press briefing earlier today, OpenAI co-founder and president Greg Brockman offered an unusually direct formulation of that message, ending the session with: “Welc
news.summary: OpenAI has announced the launch of GPT‑6 Astra, claiming it marks the beginning of artificial general intelligence. The new model promises highly autonomous systems that could surpass human performance in many economic tasks.
news.enterprise_use: S1: Review OpenAI’s new API endpoints for GPT‑6 Astra this week to assess integration possibilities with your existing SSO and identity management workflows. S2: Failure to evaluate the model could mean missing out on advanced automation that could reduce manual credential verification and anomaly detection effort. S3: JumpCloud and Freshservice will be most affected, as they can leverage the model for smarter user provisioning and incident response automation.

news.title: Gemini 3.8 text-to-speech says hello
news.summary: Google DeepMind has released Gemini 3.8, a new text‑to‑speech model that can generate spoken outputs from text. It showcases advanced voice synthesis capabilities, potentially useful for accessibility and automation in enterprise environments.
news.enterprise_use: Evaluate integrating Gemini 3.8 into your internal support tools, such as Freshservice chatbots or JumpCloud onboarding scripts, to provide dynamic voice responses for users. This could reduce manual response time and improve accessibility for employees who prefer audio communication.

news.title: Two years of OpenAI Academy

news.summary: OpenAI celebrates the two-year anniversary of its Academy, an initiative aimed at expanding AI education and skills across diverse communities. The announcement highlights the growth of AI literacy programs and outreach efforts.
news.enterprise_use: Monitor the Academy’s new course offerings for content that could inform your internal training modules. Incorporating relevant modules could accelerate skill development in your IT staff, improving adoption of AI-driven tools across your stack.

Microsoft has been in the business of education for five decades. That commitment continues today, in a technological...
The post Microsoft’s commitment for AI in education: Protecting students, strengthening learning appeared first on The Official Microsoft Blog.

news.title: Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics
news.summary_raw:
Robots are getting smarter, but how can their hardware match that growth? New Microsoft Research findings show that moving AI inference beyond the robot can improve task success, boost efficiency, and support more advanced physical AI workloads.
The post Offloaded inference for real-world physical AI robotics appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has demonstrated that offloading AI inference from robotic hardware to external processors can enhance task success rates and overall efficiency for physical AI applications. This approach allows robots to perform more complex workloads without needing heavier on-board compute.
news.enterprise_use: Consider evaluating whether offloaded inference could benefit any robotics or automation projects your team manages. Even if you don't deploy robots now, understanding this architecture could inform future decisions about hardware scaling and cloud integration for AI workloads.

news.title: Automating coherent long-form video generation
news.summary_raw: Generative AI
news.summary: Google AI has launched an automated system that generates coherent long‑form videos from textual or visual prompts. This new capability promises to streamline content production for teams that need video assets at scale.
news.enterprise_use: Monitor the release for potential integration with Google Workspace’s media tools and assess if your team’s marketing or support content could be generated more efficiently. Evaluating this tech could reduce manual video editing hours and free up IT resources for other priorities.

news.enterprise_use: Keep an eye on the Hugging Face Hub for LFM2.5-VL-DSpark release notes; it could offer a powerful foundation for future AI‑driven automation or analytics that may integrate with your existing toolchain in the next few months.

news.title: How UK AISI and EvalEval Are Making Benchmark Results Reproducible
news.summary: Hugging Face researchers AISI and EvalEval have published a methodology to make benchmark results reproducible by automating the entire evaluation pipeline. This ensures that model performance metrics can be independently verified and compared across studies.
news.enterprise_use: Note this development as it highlights the importance of reproducible evaluation when assessing AI models for internal tools. Consider integrating a similar automated benchmarking framework into your internal AI pilot programs to ensure consistent performance tracking.

news.summary_raw: With Codex, GPT-Live-1, and GPT-6 Astra, Proaction builds, operates, and sells modern fleet management faster.

news.enterprise_use: Keep an eye on OpenAI’s Codex API enhancements and pricing changes over the next three months, as these could offer new automation opportunities for your SSO and MDM workflows. A delay in evaluating Codex may mean missing out on streamlined script generation that could reduce manual configuration time.

Across industries, the conversation has shifted from what AI can do to how companies can use AI to create business value and expand what people are able to achieve. At Microsoft, we believe the organizations that succeed will be what we call Frontier Firms:...
The post What we’ve learned from Microsoft’s own AI transformation appeared first on The Official Microsoft Blog.
news.summary: Microsoft’s official blog outlines lessons from its internal AI adoption, emphasizing the shift from capability focus to business value creation and the importance of building "Frontier Firms." news.enterprise_use: Review the blog’s insights to identify potential gaps in your current AI strategy and consider integrating similar value‑driven AI initiatives across your Google Workspace, JumpCloud, and Freshservice environments. Align these lessons with your team’s roadmap to prioritize AI projects that deliver measurable business outcomes.

news.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
news.summary_raw:
Custom-made molecules are advancing medicine, materials, and agriculture, but producing them is slow and expensive. A new Nature paper highlights RetroChimera, a predictive model that helps accelerate chemical synthesis, helping researchers explore a wide range of molecules.
The post Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has published a Nature paper on RetroChimera, a predictive model that improves the synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale. The model accelerates chemical synthesis, enabling researchers to explore a broader range of compounds more efficiently.
news.enterprise_use: Watch for any future integration of RetroChimera or similar AI chemistry tools into cloud-based scientific workflows, as they could affect data storage, compute resource allocation, or collaboration platforms. Assess whether your team’s research data pipelines or third‑party SaaS services might need to accommodate larger datasets or specialized inference workloads.

news.title: GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models
news.summary_raw:
What if pathology foundation models could do more with less? GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash cut computational demands while maintaining strong performance, opening the door to larger studies and broader exploration.
The post GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash: Toward population-scale discovery with efficient pathology foundation models appeared first on Microsoft Research.
news.summary: Microsoft Research has released GigaPath-Flash and GigaTIME-Flash, efficient pathology foundation models that reduce computational demands while maintaining strong performance. These models enable larger population-scale studies and broader exploration in medical imaging.
news.enterprise_use: Check if your IT department’s data pipelines or AI workloads could integrate these models to reduce GPU costs and improve inference speed. If your team uses Azure AI or custom ML services, consider testing GigaPath-Flash in a pilot to evaluate performance gains.
